module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 62

Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy [105] from 1987.

*Reference:* [Ben Green's Open Problem 62](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.62)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
namespace Green62

/--
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_62 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime →
        let A := (Finset.range p).filter Nat.Prime
        ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < p →
          ∃ a₁ ∈ A, ∃ a₂ ∈ A, (x : ZMod p) = (a₁ * a₂ : ZMod p) := by
  sorry

end Green62

findings.description: The module docstring says "This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko, and Sárközy [105] from 1987." The bracketed label refers to the bibliography of Green's list, and the file has no bibliography of its own. In the version the file links to (open-problems.pdf, "Most recent update: December 2025"), entry [105] is T. Erdélyi's paper on unimodular zeros of self-reciprocal polynomials. The Erdős–Odlyzko–Sárközy paper is [113]. So "[105]" is a stale, dangling label that now sends readers to the wrong paper. The Lean statement is not affected.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 open problems, Problem 62, Comments: "This is a problem of Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy [113] from 1987." Bibliography: "[113] P. Erdős, A. M. Odlyzko, and A. Sárközy. On the residues of products of prime numbers, Period. Math. Hungar., 18 (1987), no. 3, 229–239." and "[105] T. Erdélyi, The number of unimodular zeros of self-reciprocal polynomials with coefficients in a finite set, Acta Arith. 176 (2016), no. 2, 177–200." (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf, December 2025 version)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "[105]" with a citation that does not depend on Green's numbering, e.g. "[EOS87]", and add the reference entry: P. Erdős, A. M. Odlyzko, A. Sárközy, On the residues of products of prime numbers, Period. Math. Hungar. 18 (1987), no. 3, 229–239. Failing that, change the label to [113].

reformulations.difference: The Lean takes primes a₁, a₂ < p (`(Finset.range p).filter Nat.Prime`) and residues x ∈ {1,…,p−1} cast into `ZMod p`, and encodes "large prime" as `∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime → …`. The literature states the Erdős–Odlyzko–Sárközy conjecture differently (Matomäki–Teräväinen, arXiv:2301.07679): E₂(q) = ℤ_q^× for all large enough primes q, i.e. every reduced residue class mod q is p₁p₂ with primes p₁, p₂ ≤ q.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, a factor equal to p is 0 in `ZMod p`, so it cannot give a nonzero x. Hence primes ≤ p and primes < p produce the same products on nonzero residues. The units of `ZMod p` are exactly the casts of 1,…,p−1. And `∀ᶠ p in atTop, (p.Prime → Q p)` is `∃ N, ∀ p ≥ N, p.Prime → Q p` (`Filter.eventually_atTop`), i.e. "for all sufficiently large primes". I proved in Lean (standard axioms only) that the file's right-hand side is equivalent to `∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ u : (ZMod p)ˣ, ∃ q₁ q₂ : ℕ, q₁.Prime ∧ q₁ ≤ p ∧ q₂.Prime ∧ q₂ ≤ p ∧ (u : ZMod p) = q₁ * q₂`. I also checked by `simp` that the body is literally "x ≡ a₁a₂ [MOD p] with primes a₁, a₂ < p".

review.notes:
`Green62.green_62` is the only declaration in the file. It states Green's Problem 62 faithfully. The right-hand side is the affirmative of Green's question, so there is no negated-conjecture issue, and `answer(sorry)` sits outside all quantifiers.

Numerical sanity check: I ran a Perl search and cross-checked it with `#eval` of a Boolean copy of the Lean body built on the same Finset `A`. The property fails for p = 2, 3, 5, …, 191 (31 primes in that range) and again for p = 397 and p = 401; for example, p = 401 misses x = 385. It holds for every prime 409 ≤ p ≤ 15000. So the `∀ᶠ` ('large prime') qualifier is essential, and the file includes it; a version over all primes would be false.

Status: `research open` matches Green's December 2025 list, whose only update is Matomäki–Teräväinen's k = 3 result. It also matches Matomäki–Teräväinen (Crelle 2024), who write that the two-prime case 'remains open even under GRH'. I found no later resolution on arXiv.

The original 1987 paper is only available as an image scan that I could not OCR. I relied on Green's wording, which is the cited source, and on Matomäki–Teräväinen's exact restatement of the conjecture. Both agree with the Lean.
